newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges rise on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges rise on short-covering.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges rose for a second day running on Friday on the back of short-covering by market players while cargoes were steady with tight avails supporting the market in the absence of fresh deals, traders said.

After an early trade at $85.50 fob ARA, high sulphur fuel barges began inching upwards at 50-cent intervals from $86 to $87.50, up to $1 over the highest deal on Thursday when barges finally broke through the week's recent trend of trade of $85/$86 a tonne.
Most traders attributed the rise to improving bunker demand and buying to cover short positions with a tight cargo market also contributing to support levels.
"There's a rise in demand but not many people offering," one trader said.
Traders said high sulphur cargoes were largely unchanged with offers at $84/$85 cif on the offer side with buyers in the $81 region.

Two cargoes of lower quality material were heard resold recently at a discount by a trader to the original holder after no other buyers came around. The seller was offering earlier in the $82 cif mark.
Russian high sulphur straight run continued to be tight, with E-4 and M-40 particularly scarce. M-100 was being offered largely steady at two means +$4.
"E-4 and M-40 are not really seen, the only talk is on M-100 and that's at two means plus $4ish," one broker said.
A second trader said he was not surprised with that number given that demand for straight-run continues.

A northern European electricity utility that was looking for a small piece for one of its smaller units has withdrawn its offer, saying it had nothing to do with prices but a change in its consumption scenario for that particular location.
